newsitem.title: USA: Hearing set on Great Western merger vote on May 30.
newsitem.headline: Hearing set on Great Western merger vote on May 30.

text.p: A Delaware Chancery Court judge has scheduled a hearing May 30 on whether shareholders of Great Western Financial Corp should be allowed to vote at the annual meeting June 13 on a proposed merger with Washington Mutual Inc.

According to court papers made available to Reuters on Wednesday, Vice Chancellor Jack Jacobs of the Delaware Chancery Court also approved a request by Washington Mutual to be an intervenor at the hearing.
Washington Mutual said in court papers it had "important distinct interests in the subject matter of this action" and that its merger proposal calls for a shareholder vote "as soon as practicable."

The timing of the vote is opposed by rival bidder H.F. Ahmanson & Co, which wants Jacobs to delay a shareholder vote on the merger until six weeks after the annual meeting. Ahmanson claims it has enough proxies to replace three Great Western directors with Ahmanson's slate on June 13.
On Tuesday, the Great Western board rejected Ahmanson's offer of about $50.40 a share versus $50.52 a share from Washington Mutual.
By delaying a shareholder vote, Ahmanson hopes its slate, if seated, will have time to influence the remaining Great Western board members.
